targetText: But all sources rightly believe that the Qassamist rising, sparked off by Sheikh Izz al-Din al-Qassam was the real start of the 1936 revolt.
summary: Sheikh Izz al-Din al-Qassam's guerrilla organizing among rural and displaced workers marked the qualitative transformation into armed anti-colonial revolt.
explanation: Al-Qassam rejected the futile petitioning of the traditional urban notables and instead mobilized impoverished displaced fellahin and dockworkers around Haifa. His martyrdom in the battle of Ya'bad in November 1935 transformed him into an enduring symbol of popular revolutionary armed resistance.

targetText: However, the report of the Royal Commission (Lord Peel) which Yehuda Bauer regards as one of the more authoritative sources written about the Palestine problem, sidesteps (ignores) these immediate causes for the outbreak of the revolt, and attributes the outbreak to two main causes: the Arabs' desire to win national independence and their aversion to, and fear of, the establishment of the "Jewish national home" in Palestine.
summary: Official British colonial reports deliberately obscured concrete material dispossessions by reducing the revolt to abstract political sentiments.
explanation: Colonial commissions systematically ignored empirical socio-economic drivers such as land evictions, starvation wages, and monopolistic concessions, framing the revolt as irrational racial friction to absolve British imperial policy of culpability.

targetText: In fact the real cause of the revolt was the fact that the acute conflicts involved in the transformation of Palestinian society from an Arab agricultural-feudal-clerical one into a Zionist (Western) industrial bourgeois one, had reached their climax, as we have already seen.
summary: The 1936 revolt was the explosive culmination of Palestine's violent socio-economic transformation under British-backed settler industrialization.
explanation: Kanafani demonstrates historical materialism: the uprising was the objective result of structural contradictions reaching boiling point as indigenous agricultural society was uprooted by colonial capitalist industrialization.

targetText: it is the failure to grasp the dialectical connection between religion and nationalist tendencies that is responsible for the belittling of the importance of the Qassamist movement.
summary: Religious phraseology expressed deep anti-imperialist class aspirations rather than clerical obscurantism.
explanation: Bourgeois and Western commentators frequently dismissed al-Qassam's movement as mere religious fanaticism. Kanafani explains that among peasant masses in pre-capitalist societies, religious discourse was the historical language through which revolutionary anti-colonial consciousness and sacrifice were articulated.

targetText: Even when the general strike was declared on 19th April 1936 the leadership of the nationalist movement lagged behind. However, they soon got on the bandwagon before it left them behind
summary: The historic general strike began spontaneously from below, forcing reluctant traditional leaders to scramble to keep up.
explanation: The six-month general strike was initiated by urban transportation workers, youth, and popular national committees in Jaffa and Nablus. The traditional aristocratic leadership joined only when it realized the mass movement would bypass them entirely.

targetText: The petty-bourgeoisie in general (small traders, shopkeepers, teachers, civil servants and craftsmen) had no leadership. As a class they had had no influence and no importance under the Turkish regime
summary: The urban petty bourgeoisie lacked autonomous class organization, leaving them politically subordinate to feudal notables.
explanation: Although shopkeepers, civil servants, and teachers formed the core urban activists of the strike, their absence of independent political leadership left them subordinated to the conservative Arab Higher Committee.

targetText: The British Emergency Regulations played an effective role. AI-Sifri cites a group of sentences passed at the time to show how unjust these regulations were: "six years' imprisonment for possessing a revolver- 12 years far possessing a bomb - five years with hard labour for possessing 12 bullets
summary: Draconian British martial law imposed extreme sentences and collective punishment to terrorize the population.
explanation: British military tribunals enforced sweeping penalties, execution for weapon possession, and punitive demolition of villages, establishing a framework of colonial terror later inherited by the Israeli occupation apparatus.

summary: Reactionary Arab elites secretly orchestrated appeals from British client kings to shut down the general strike without admitting their betrayal.
explanation: Terrified of the popular armed rebellion, the feudal Arab Higher Committee conspired with British officials and Arab monarchs (in Transjordan, Iraq, and Saudi Arabia) to fabricate a royal appeal that gave the notables an excuse to call off the general strike.

targetText: the Peel Commission, which, published on 7th July 1937, recommended partition and the establishment of a Jewish state.
summary: Britain's 1937 Peel Commission recommended the partition of Palestine, triggering the second and most militant phase of armed insurrection.
explanation: The recommendation to carve up Palestine and award the most fertile agricultural regions to a minority settler population exposed the full reality of British colonial intentions, driving the rural masses into full-scale armed guerrilla war.

targetText: the government announced the recruitment of 1240 Zionists as additional policemen armed with army rifles. A month later the figure rose to 286386 and British officers played a prominent role in leading Zionist groups in attacks on Palestinian Arab villages.
summary: British military authorities armed and mobilized Zionist paramilitary forces as colonial auxiliaries to suppress Arab resistance.
explanation: British military intelligence (under figures like Orde Wingate) organized the Special Night Squads, training and arming Haganah fighters to launch night ambushes against Palestinian villages. This British-Zionist military collaboration established the operational foundation of the future Israeli military apparatus.

Later, all were forbidden to carry their identity cards, so that the authorities should not be able to distinguish a townsman from a countryman.
summary: The adoption of the rural peasant keffiyeh across urban centers symbolized the revolutionary hegemony of the rural masses.
explanation: When British military forces profiled rural fighters by their peasant headwear, the revolutionary leadership ordered urban merchants and effendis to discard the Ottoman tarbush and wear the peasant keffiyeh. This striking cultural mandate unified town and countryside around the militant peasantry.

summary: The material disparity between advanced settler industrial organization and traditional agrarian society doomed the revolt in the absence of a revolutionary vanguard.
explanation: Kanafani draws the overarching historical materialist balance sheet: while Palestinian peasants fought with unmatched heroism, the immense disparity in industrial organization, British imperial military superiority, and the treachery of traditional elites produced defeat in the absence of a vanguard party.
